reference.notes:
I implemented the spec in `packages/core/src/selection/`, and every test now passes. The whole package suite ran 149 tests with 149 passing, which includes all 71 in `hidden-categories-confirmed/` and the existing bounty and handle tests. `npm test` also passes, and its coverage report shows 100% for all of the new files.

I changed only the five selection files and kept every exported name and signature.

- **`facts.ts`**: `factsFor` builds the facts from the issue and the `now` you pass in. A missing, unreadable or future date counts as 0 days. Due dates and releases are counted in UTC calendar days. Priority is trimmed before it's looked up, and the lookup ignores built-in object keys like `constructor`.
- **`rules.ts`**: `all`, `any`, `silent` and `signal` return plain values. `evaluate` checks every child even after one fails, and only calls `describe` when that signal's test matched.
- **`signals.ts`**: each signal uses the wording, singular/plural forms and thresholds the spec sets out. `deadlineWithin` describes whichever of the due date or the release is sooner inside the window; a tie goes to the due date.
- **`categories.ts`**: the six categories are built through a small `category()` helper I added. It fills in any threshold missing from what a rule is given with that category's default, so calling a shipped rule with incomplete thresholds still works. `resolveCategories` keeps the default for an override that is null, undefined or not finite, and ignores unknown keys and category ids. `createClassifier` builds each enabled rule once, when it is created.
